name: R2-BRIDGE-01 -- Retention Feasibility Bridge, Phase-0 contract

scientific_question.primary: Does using the frozen causal predictor decayed_transition/decay=0.99 as an online retention signal reduce expert-memory traffic (miss_bytes_per_decode_step) relative to the frozen strong causal baseline B_selected(M), on a new, prospectively-specified, held-out BRIDGE corpus?
scientific_question.framing: A replay-level feasibility question. NOT a runtime-speed question -- no tokens/s or latency claim is in scope.
scientific_question.relationship_to_r2_10: R2-10 measured prediction quality (recall@k of the predictor against the next routing event) and never evaluated the predictor as a retention/eviction signal. This bridge asks the retention question for the first time, using the exact same frozen predictor, without reopening or reinterpreting any R2-10 evidence.
scientific_question.relationship_to_r2_11: This bridge's outcome may justify PROSPECTIVELY proposing a new, separate R2-11 protocol. It can never retroactively satisfy, promote, or reverse the ORIGINAL frozen R2-10 decision (R2-11 NOT PROPOSED under decision_rules.json as it stood at R2-10 closure).

baseline_binding.name: B_selected(M)
baseline_binding.global_lru_role: descriptive reference only, if useful; never the primary comparator

in_scope: design and freeze this contract and all referenced sub-contracts
write and run first-class leakage/causality, memory-correctness, determinism, and control-equivalence tests (synthetic traces and/or existing DEV traces only, per dev_holdout_separation.json)
independently re-verify that R2-10 and R2-09B frozen contracts/digests have not drifted
explicitly_out_of_scope: modifying R2-10 or changing its Category B status
using the R2-10 EVAL set to tune the retention policy
